title: The Quiet House

clips.speaker: narrator
clips.text: You think I am mad, but my mind is well. My illness made my senses stronger, especially my hearing. I hear everything in heaven and on earth. Listen, and tell me how calmly I explain it. I loved the old man who shared my house. He never hurt me, and I wanted none of his money. Only his pale blue eye with its cloudy covering troubled me. It looked like a vulture's eye, you understand? I had to get rid of that eye. At midnight, for seven nights, I silently opened his door. I shone a thin line of light from my lantern. His eye stayed shut, so I could do nothing. You see, I hated his eye, not him. On night eight, I smiled at how patiently I worked. Then my thumb slipped against the lantern's catch.

clips.speaker: narrator
clips.text: You must admire how I stood still for an hour. He stayed awake, listening, then gave a low, frightened groan. I knew that sound from my own nights without sleep. Finally, I let a little light out of the lantern. It fell straight onto his eye. That eye was now completely open. I heard his heart beating softly, but very quickly. It sounded like a watch covered in cotton. It grew faster and louder; a neighbour might hear! I rushed inside, and he gave one sharp scream. I dragged him down and pulled the heavy bed over him. When his heart stopped, I checked: he was dead. I hid his body under three boards in the floor. I put them back perfectly, leaving no marks or stains. You wouldn't expect a madman to work so neatly!

clips.speaker: narrator
clips.text: Three police officers came knocking at four in the morning. A neighbour had heard a scream, but I welcomed them. I said a bad dream had made me cry out. The old man was visiting the country, I told them. After showing them every room, I put chairs in his bedroom. I sat right above the body; you see my courage? As they chatted, a ringing sound began in my ears. Then, below their voices, I heard that soft, quick beating.

clips.speaker: narrator
clips.text: I spoke louder, stood up, and walked around the room. I dragged my chair across the boards, but the beating grew louder. They kept smiling and talking, as if they heard nothing. But they must hear it; they knew what I'd done! Their smiles were laughing at me. How could you expect me to bear it? "I killed him!" I screamed. "Pull up the floorboards, here under my chair! That is the sound of his horrible heart beating!"
